title: Canonical affinization of a qcqs algebraic stack
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $\mathcal U$ be an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack] whose structural map $\mathcal U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Put $R=\Gamma(\mathcal U,\mathcal O_{\mathcal U})$, with structure sheaf and global sections as in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. There is a unique $k$-morphism up to $2$-isomorphism $a_{\mathcal U}:\mathcal U\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] whose restriction along every scheme morphism $u:V\to\mathcal U$ corresponds to the ring map $u^*:R\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ under [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. The morphism $a_{\mathcal U}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Under the canonical $R\simeq\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)$, its map on global functions is $\mathrm{id}_R$. In particular no finite-type, separated-diagonal or moduli-space hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 075S, lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence (2), applied to the affinization map into an affine scheme. Construction: smooth descent of the scheme affine-target correspondence (existing node lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme); it is also the canonical morphism used by Alper Remark 4.1.3 and Remark 5.1.2.

proof.text: Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], an element $r\in R$ is a compatible family $(r_x)$, indexed by objects $x$ of $\mathcal U$ over schemes $V$, with $r_x\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, and the ring operations are pointwise. Evaluation gives a ring map $e_x:R\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] it determines a unique scheme map $a_x:V\to Y$ with $a_x^\sharp=e_x$. The structure map $k\to R$ is the family of structural pullbacks $k\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$; let $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the corresponding affine-scheme map. Since $(ga_x)^\sharp=a_x^\sharp g^\sharp$ is the structural map $k\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, the same bijection for the target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that $ga_x$ is the structure morphism of $V$: each $a_x$ is a $k$-morphism, an object of $h_Y(V)$. For an arrow $x'\to x$ over $v:V'\to V$, compatibility gives $e_{x'}=v^*e_x$, so the same bijection gives $a_{x'}=a_xv$. Send $x$ to $a_x$ and this arrow to the unique arrow over $v$ in the discrete fibred category $h_Y$. These assignments respect identities and composition, and hence give a functor $a:\mathcal U\to h_Y$ over the base by the morphism convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Its restriction to every scheme test is the required map.

source.place: Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine); stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06TV (definition-structure-sheaf). The objectwise assembly is written here from the definitions.

proof.text: By step 1, for each object $x/V$ the composite $ga_x$ is the structural map of $V$; thus $ga$ is the given structural morphism $p$ of $\mathcal U$, and $a$ is a $k$-morphism. If $b$ is a $k$-morphism with the specified restrictions, then $b(x)^\sharp=e_x=a_x^\sharp$, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] gives $b(x)=a_x$ for every $x$. The target fibres have only identity arrows, so $b$ and $a$ also agree on arrows, and these equalities give the unique $2$-isomorphism $b\simeq a$, compatible with every arrow. This is exactly the asserted uniqueness up to $2$-isomorphism, read in the definitions of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] and [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine), uniqueness, together with the stated definitions of global sections and functors to a discrete fibred category.

proof.text: Under $R\simeq\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ the pullback $a^*(r)$ has component $a_x^*(r)=e_x(r)=r_x$ at every object $x/V$. Equality of global sections is equality of these compatible families by [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Therefore $a^*=\mathrm{id}_R$. This also fixes the normalization of the map, without choosing an atlas or a presentation.

source.place: Tag 06TV (definition-structure-sheaf), global sections as compatible families; schemes.tex Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine).

proof.text: The affine scheme $Y$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Hence $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-separated as a scheme morphism by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], so its diagonal $d:Y\to Y\times_kY$ is quasi-compact. The source of $d$ is again $Y$, so clause (1) makes $d$ quasi-separated too, and clause (3) keeps both properties for every scheme base change $h_T:A_T=T\times_{Y\times_kY}Y\to T$. Schemes are regarded as discrete fibred groupoids, so this $2$-fibre product is the scheme fibre product: $d$ is representable. To pass to the algebraic-space predicates of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], let $h:A\to T$ be a quasi-compact scheme morphism and $C\to T$ a quasi-compact algebraic space, with representable surjective etale $h_U\to C$, $U$ a quasi-compact scheme, as in that definition. Then $h_{A\times_TU}\to A\times_TC$ is representable, etale and surjective, since its fibre product with any $h_{T'}\to A\times_TC$ is $h_{T'}\times_Ch_U$. The scheme $A\times_TU$ is quasi-compact by clauses (3) and (2); hence $A\times_TC$ is quasi-compact, and $h$ is quasi-compact as a map of algebraic spaces. Apply this to $h_T$ and to its scheme diagonal, whose sheaf fibre products are scheme fibre products: each $h_T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated as a map of algebraic spaces. Thus $d$ is quasi-separated as a representable stack morphism, and is quasi-compact as a stack morphism by [lem-sfb-representable-stack-quasicompact-tests]. The products used here and below exist as algebraic stacks by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products].

Factor $a$ as $\mathcal U\xrightarrow{\gamma}\mathcal U\times_kY\xrightarrow{q}Y$, where $\gamma=(1,a)$ and $q$ is the second projection. The graph square with bottom arrow $d:Y\to Y\times_kY$ and right arrow $(a\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2)$ is $2$-cartesian: an object of its pullback is $(x,y,\alpha:a(x)\simeq y)$ and is uniquely identified, over $x$, with $(x,a(x),1)$. Thus $\gamma$ is a base change of the quasi-compact $d$ of step 4, and $q$ is a base change of the quasi-compact structural map $p$. Base change preserves quasi-compactness directly from [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]: testing the pullback at a quasi-compact stack is testing the original morphism at the composite map. Composition preserves it by testing $q$ first, then $\gamma$ at the resulting quasi-compact stack. Hence $a=q\gamma$ is quasi-compact. The graph and the identifications use the explicit $2$-fibre product of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 050Y (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence), graph argument; Tags 050V and 050W, whose base-change and composition assertions are proved here directly from the testing definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-quasiseparated-cancellation] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to $\mathcal U\xrightarrow{a}Y\xrightarrow{g}\operatorname{Spec}k$. The composite is the given quasi-separated $p$ by step 2. Its other hypothesis is quasi-separatedness of $\Delta_g=d$ as a representable morphism, established on all scheme tests in step 4. Therefore $a$ is quasi-separated. Together with steps 1--5 this proves every clause. In particular the argument used neither finite type nor a separated diagonal nor a moduli-space property.
